name: java-guide
Java guardrails for `.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, or when Java is mentioned. Applies to Java 17+, Spring Boot, Maven/Gradle, enterprise applications.

Prefer immutability (records, `final` fields, unmodifiable collections), explicit types, boundary validation (`Objects.requireNonNull`), composition, and standard-library solutions (`java.util`, `java.time`, `java.nio`). Use Java 17+ (LTS) with preview features disabled in production. Manage dependencies with Maven (`pom.xml`) or Gradle (`build.gradle.kts`). Pin dependency versions explicitly (no dynamic versions like `1.+`). Run `mvn dependency:analyze` or `gradle dependencies` to detect unused/undeclared deps. Check for vulnerabilities: `mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check`.

Follow [Google Java Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html). Classes: `PascalCase`; methods/fields: `camelCase`; constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`; packages: lowercase `com.company.project.module`. One top-level class per file (name matches filename). Use `var` for local variables only when the type is obvious from the right side. No wildcard imports (`import java.util.*` is forbidden).

Use `record` for immutable data carriers instead of manual POJOs; add compact constructors for validation. Use `sealed` classes/interfaces for restricted type hierarchies; they enable exhaustive `switch` expressions with pattern matching. Use streams for transformations, not for side effects. Never call `Optional.get()` -- use `orElseThrow()`, `orElse()`, `map()`, `flatMap()`. Do not use `Optional` as a method parameter or field type (only as a return type). Avoid parallel streams unless measured to be faster (overhead is real). Prefer `toList()` (Java 16+) over `collect(Collectors.toList())`. Always use try-with-resources for `AutoCloseable` types. Never rely on `finalize()` (deprecated and unreliable). Close resources in reverse order of acquisition.

Project conventions: packages map to bounded contexts, not top-level technical layers. Test structure mirrors source structure; keep `resources/` flat and use `db/migration/` for schema changes. Layout: `java/com/company/project/` (Application.java, config/, controller/, service/, repository/, model/, dto/, exception/); `db/migration/`; `test/java/com/company/project/`; `target/` (gitignored).

Tests: Test files mirror source under `src/test/java`; class names `ClassNameTest`, not `TestClassName`. Test methods: `<REDACTED_USER> void shouldDescribeBehavior()`. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` for complex scenarios, `<REDACTED_USER>` to group related tests. Coverage target: >80% for business logic, >60% overall. Prefer AssertJ over JUnit assertions. Use mocks, verify interactions, test exceptions and parameterized cases.

mvn clean install              # Build and install locally
mvn test                       # Run all tests
mvn verify                     # Run tests + integration tests
mvn dependency:tree            # Show dependency tree
mvn dependency:analyze         # Find unused/undeclared deps
mvn spotbugs:check             # Static analysis
mvn checkstyle:check           # Style check
./gradlew build                # Full build with tests
./gradlew test                 # Run unit tests
./gradlew check                # Run all verification tasks
./gradlew dependencies         # Show dependency tree
./gradlew jacocoTestReport     # Generate coverage report

See [references/patterns.md](references/patterns.md) for Spring patterns, streams, Optional, and builders; [Google Java Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html); [Effective Java (3rd Edition)](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/effective-java/9780134686097/); [Java Records (JEP 395)](https://openjdk.org/jeps/395); [Sealed Classes (JEP 409)](https://openjdk.org/jeps/409); [Pattern Matching for switch (JEP 441)]
